headline: High risk of prompt injection and cascading error: Haystack’s MCP/REST outputs can be fed into AI Engineering Hub workflows, while Haystack’s broad egress raises leakage and compliance exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Haystack exposes MCP servers and REST APIs, so its outputs can be bridged into ai-engineering-hub workflows if the pair is wired together. ai-engineering-hub is an agents/RAG repo with no documented isolation or provenance controls, so prompt-like content could be treated as instructions. The pathway is plausible but not directly documented.
conditions: IF Haystack outputs are copied into ai-engineering-hub prompts or files
IF an MCP server is configured to pass untrusted content without provenance tags
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of external text into prompts
Add a provenance prefix to all Haystack outputs
Require manual review before re-prompting on generated content
Use separate workspaces for the two agents
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization middleware

B_data_leakage.rationale: Haystack has broad network egress and can call REST/MCP endpoints, so any sensitive context it receives may leave the local boundary. ai-engineering-hub shows no data classes touched and no egress, so the main leakage risk is one-way from the pair into Haystack’s outbound calls. The shared-data pathway is plausible but not evidenced as default.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are supplied to Haystack
IF Haystack is configured to forward retrieved text to external REST or MCP endpoints
mitigations: Do not send secrets or regulated data to Haystack
Restrict Haystack to local-only endpoints
Review outbound destinations before enabling the pair
Separate sensitive and non-sensitive corpora
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents can participate in mutable workflows: ai-engineering-hub is an agents/RAG repo that may write artifacts, and Haystack can call REST APIs and MCP servers. If they target the same workspace or shared mutable resource, write conflicts are plausible. No locking or coordination primitive is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or shared API resource
IF no external lock or transaction layer is configured
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Avoid concurrent runs on the same dataset
Check for existing file before overwrite
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Haystack is a search-RAG system, so it can pass retrieved or generated text downstream, and ai-engineering-hub is an agents/RAG repo that may consume such outputs as prompts or facts. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions or generated artifacts. Because no verification step is documented, the safer choice is high.
conditions: IF Haystack output is used as direct input to ai-engineering-hub
IF the downstream step does not verify citations or source provenance
mitigations: Require source links for every retrieved claim
Insert a human verification step before actioning outputs
Compare outputs against original documents
Limit Haystack to retrieval-only mode
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, EU PII, or residency-sensitive data class is documented for either agent, so a compliance breach is not established. Haystack does touch anonymous usage statistics and has broad egress, while ai-engineering-hub shows no data classes touched. The mismatch is therefore limited and only becomes relevant if regulated data is introduced.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is routed through Haystack
IF retention or residency rules are imposed on data not listed in the profiles
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document retention settings for Haystack
Disable analytics on sensitive deployments
Review data-processing notices
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls
